# uem_smart_group (Resource)

Manages a smart group in Workspace ONE UEM (MDM API v1). A smart group either matches devices by criteria (`criteria_type = "All"`) or lists users and devices explicitly (`criteria_type = "UserDevice"`).

## Criteria types

- With `criteria_type = "All"`, the criteria attributes (`platforms`, `ownerships`, `models`, `management_types`, `enrollment_categories`, `cpu_architectures`, `organization_group_ids`, `user_group_ids`, `tag_ids`, `operating_systems`) select devices. `user_additions` and `device_additions` are meant for `criteria_type = "UserDevice"` instead.
- With `criteria_type = "UserDevice"`, members are listed with `user_additions` and `device_additions`. The criteria attributes are meant for `criteria_type = "All"` instead.
- `user_exclusions`, `device_exclusions` and `user_group_exclusions` are valid with either type.
- The provider does not enforce the `criteria_type`/attribute pairing itself at `terraform plan` time; UEM validates it at apply. With `criteria_type = "All"` and no criteria configured at all, the smart group matches every device in its managing organization group; `terraform plan` still warns about that case.

## Drift and comparison

- Every list-like attribute is a set, so order never causes a diff.
- `criteria_type`, `platforms`, `models`, `management_types`, `enrollment_categories`, `cpu_architectures` and `operating_systems` are read back exactly as UEM returns them. They are not case-insensitive: UEM echoes back whatever casing you configure, and sending it a different casing on update can fail (a lowercase platform returned an HTTP 500 in testing).
- `ownerships` is read back exactly as UEM returns it, like the other criteria attributes above. When `ownerships` is not set, UEM stores `allownerships`. That server default reads back as unset, so it causes no diff.
- `devices_count`, `assignments_count` and `exclusions_count` are refreshed on every read and never cause a diff.
- Every update sends the whole smart group. Emptying a set (for example `platforms = []`, or removing it) leaves that field out of the request, because the UEM API model omits empty lists; UEM then keeps the field's existing value rather than clearing it. **`terraform plan`/`apply` reject this at plan time** with an error naming the attribute, instead of silently keeping the old value or reporting a confusing inconsistent-result error after the fact. To actually clear a criterion, member or exclusion set, remove it in the UEM console, or recreate the resource (`terraform apply -replace=<this resource's address>`).

## Manufacturer/OEM and Model criteria

The OEM and Model criterion (`OEMAndModels` in the UEM API) is not currently supported by this resource; it is deferred. If a smart group has it set in UEM, reads emit a warning and it is not imported into state. Updates keep the value UEM already has.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "organization_group_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Numeric id of the organization group that manages the smart group"
}

# Criteria-based smart group: every corporate-dedicated macOS device on
# a macOS version later than 13.0.
resource "uem_smart_group" "macs" {
  name                    = "terraform_example_macs"
  managed_by_org_group_id = var.organization_group_id
  criteria_type           = "All"

  platforms  = ["AppleOsX"]
  ownerships = ["CorporateDedicated"]

  operating_systems = [
    {
      device_type = "AppleOsX"
      operator    = "GreaterThan"
      value       = "13.0"
    },
  ]
}

# Explicit-membership smart group.
resource "uem_smart_group" "pilot" {
  name                    = "terraform_example_pilot"
  managed_by_org_group_id = var.organization_group_id
  criteria_type           = "UserDevice"

  device_additions  = ["1001", "1002"]
  device_exclusions = ["1003"]
}

output "macs_smart_group_uuid" {
  description = "Smart group UUID assigned by UEM"
  value       = uem_smart_group.macs.uuid
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `criteria_type` (String) `All` (match devices by the criteria attributes) or `UserDevice` (explicit `user_additions`/`device_additions`). Read back exactly as UEM returns it; UEM validates the value.
- `managed_by_org_group_id` (String) Numeric id of the organization group that manages the smart group. Must be numeric (validated at plan time). Changing it replaces the smart group.
- `name` (String) Smart group name.

### Optional

- `cpu_architectures` (Set of String) Device CPU architectures to match. Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `device_additions` (Set of String) Ids of devices added explicitly. Used only with `criteria_type = "UserDevice"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `device_exclusions` (Set of String) Ids of devices excluded. Valid with either `criteria_type`.
- `enrollment_categories` (Set of String) Enrollment categories to match (for example `DepEnrolled`). Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `management_types` (Set of String) Management types to match (for example `MdmEnrolled`). Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `models` (Set of String) Device models to match (for example `iPad`). Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `operating_systems` (Attributes Set) Operating system version rules to match. Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing. Every field is read back exactly as UEM returns it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--operating_systems))
- `organization_group_ids` (Set of String) Numeric ids of organization groups whose devices match. Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `ownerships` (Set of String) Device ownership types to match (for example `CorporateDedicated`). Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing. Read back exactly as UEM returns it. When unset, UEM stores `allownerships`; that server default is read back as unset, so it causes no diff.
- `platforms` (Set of String) Device platforms to match (for example `AppleOsX`). Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `tag_ids` (Set of String) Numeric ids of tags whose devices match. Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `user_additions` (Set of String) Ids of users added explicitly. Used only with `criteria_type = "UserDevice"`; UEM validates the pairing.
- `user_exclusions` (Set of String) Ids of users excluded. Valid with either `criteria_type`.
- `user_group_exclusions` (Set of String) Ids of user groups excluded. Valid with either `criteria_type`.
- `user_group_ids` (Set of String) Numeric ids of user groups whose devices match. Used only with `criteria_type = "All"`; UEM validates the pairing.

### Read-Only

- `assignments_count` (Number) Number of entities the smart group is assigned to, refreshed on every read.
- `devices_count` (Number) Number of devices in the smart group, refreshed on every read.
- `exclusions_count` (Number) Number of entities the smart group is excluded from, refreshed on every read.
- `id` (String) Numeric smart group identifier assigned by UEM.
- `managed_by_org_group_name` (String) Name of the managing organization group, as reported by UEM.
- `managed_by_org_group_uuid` (String) UUID of the managing organization group, as reported by UEM.
- `uuid` (String) Smart group UUID assigned by UEM.

<a id="nestedatt--operating_systems"></a>
### Nested Schema for `operating_systems`

Required:

- `device_type` (String) Device type (platform) the rule applies to.
- `operator` (String) Comparison operator (for example `GreaterThan`).
- `value` (String) Operating system version compared against.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax. The id is either the numeric smart group id or the smart group UUID (matched case-insensitively):

```shell
#!/bin/bash
# Import an existing Workspace ONE smart group into Terraform

# Import by numeric smart group id or by smart group UUID
# Usage: terraform import uem_smart_group.example "<id>"
# Usage: terraform import uem_smart_group.example "<uuid>"

terraform import uem_smart_group.example "12345"
terraform import uem_smart_group.example "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
```
